claim: CGEL infers from the definiteness of the office that bare role NPs invariably allow substitution of a corresponding NP with the.
evidence_summary: ASU reports a shared appointment. Hold team, meeting and date fixed. Compare “Faatulu became co-captain of the team that day, and so did Peck” with “Faatulu became the co-captain of the team that day, and so did Peck”. Both versions are constructed.
finding: The bare form readily assigns the office to both players. The definite counterpart invites a single-holder reading, though a salient office may sustain a shared-role reading. The attestation establishes shared tenure. Preservation of the reading under insertion is a judgment.
inference: Does an identifiable office guarantee that adding the preserves a bare role reading?

evidence.source: Arizona State University, Sun Devil Athletics. Jolynn Faatulu Overcomes Injuries to Shine.
evidence.passage: §8.5(a), p. 409, discussion of [19i–iii]. The office is “invariably definite”. The inference to substitution is signalled by “therefore invariably replaceable”. The examples concern the office of treasurer.
evidence.example: The report says Faatulu “was named co-captain along with fellow junior Jamie Peck”. It never supplies a definite counterpart in this context.
evidence.establishes: Attests a bare role with two officeholders. The two versions with became in the audit are constructed comparative judgments.
evidence.locator: Paragraph naming fellow junior Jamie Peck.
